description: Skelet AF-06-i bounded video-frame evidence: mapping, budgets, provenance without a decoder

compatibility.instructions: Does adding video-frame-evidence.ts plus its test and one CI line change any existing contract, pipeline, envelope, migration, or dependency? New module only; jpeg-evidence reused read-only; no new dependency. Do existing callers keep working?

correctness.instructions: Is the module factually correct: fps/duration/count consistency within one frame, exact whole-ms mapping (incl. fractional NTSC fps), deterministic uniform selection with boundary coverage and single-slot guard, JPEG structural + dimension + budget authentication, strictly increasing refs with timestamp cross-check, digest-bound record? Is decoder absence an honest documented boundary rather than a hidden gap?

evidence.instructions: Are the 6 tests sufficient: normalized identity, 12 malformed cases plus over-budget area, exact mapping incl. NTSC, deterministic selection incl. endpoints/singles/repeat, corruption and dimension-disagreement rejection, digest determinism with substitution/order/duplicate/empty/time rejection? Full lens suite green with typecheck/lint clean?

reliability.instructions: Any nondeterminism: pure functions over explicit inputs, fixed timestamps in tests, sorted deterministic selection? Any unhandled edge (zero frames, maxFrames 1, fractional fps)?

scope.instructions: Anything beyond the frame-evidence slice: container decoding, report integration, surfaces, paid services, or unrelated refactors? Is follow-up integration (report assembly attachment) correctly left to AF-06-ii?

security.instructions: Does the module weaken any control: untrusted specs fail closed, frames structurally validated before evidence, budgets enforced, digests bind identity and mapping, no network/codec/secrets? Any confusion between declared and observed data?

state.change: AF-06-i: video-frame-evidence mapping/budget/provenance module with 6 tests; no decoder, no new dependency, report integration deferred to AF-06-ii.
